criteria.ambient_scope: Each dispatch creates a request scope bundling the shared budget with an abort signal and an escalation log, and the SQL and fetch adapters look it up implicitly, so peer disconnect or process shutdown retires every live operation on its own terms with a per-operation unknown-write result and escalation entry; caller-supplied bounds continue to combine by taking the lesser of the bound and the budget remainder.
criteria.outer_race: The dispatcher merely times the handler as a whole against the request budget, and on timeout emits one bounded reply plus one request-wide escalation while the handler finishes in the background unseen, meaning nested operations complete with no individual unknown-write result and no escalation entry of their own.

propagation.instructions: How should dispatch forward disconnect and shutdown expiry to the operations a handler has in flight?

criteria.new_failure: Mint a dedicated catalogue failure such as sql::operation_unknown and list it in the emits of each budgeted SQL call, which surfaces boundary expiry directly in the checked error union but forces catalogue regeneration, checker and emitter work, and re-migration of current examples in other lanes.
criteria.reuse_query_failed: Express SQL boundary expiry with the presently emitted sql::query_failed failure and a documented code string (operation identifies the call, code says budget), avoiding all catalogue, checker, and emitter edits; Can code branches on the code string while the adapter converts the shared unknown-write marker into that domain value.

sql_failure.instructions: What failure value should a SQL call produce when its visible boundary returns at the bound and the native query remains owned?

criteria.status_400: Reply to a body read that exceeds its stall bound with the established fixed 400 used for body read failures, keeping the rejected-status union as it is and handling stalls identically to damaged bodies.
criteria.status_408: Reply to a body read that exceeds its stall bound with a fixed 408 Request Timeout, adding 408 to the rejected-status union, while body read failures continue to yield 400 and oversize bodies continue to yield 413.

stall_status.instructions: What status fits bounded ingress when a body read passes its stall bound?

state: The Can toolchain emits TypeScript adapters that execute natively on Bun 1.4.2 with no outside users and no duty to preserve old behavior. Executed probes settle the key facts: on PostgreSQL, MySQL, and SQLite, Bun.SQL Query.cancel only toggles a client-side flag as each backend proceeds to full completion, and a cancel issued before execution leaves the await unsettled forever, so SQL follows the cancel-absent branch where the user-facing boundary answers at the operation bound, native execution stays owned through settlement, and the reported outcome stays honestly unknown under supervisor escalation. The serve-side Request.signal fires quickly after the peer disconnects yet terminates nothing itself, making it a disconnect observation rather than an interruption. The completed E01 foundation contributes a single shared budget per request whose effective deadline is the lesser of the operation bound and the remaining budget, an immutable unknown-write marker carrying commit unknown, owned, and supervisor escalation that SQL, fetch, actions, S3, and workers all share, close paths that drain by default, and leases immune to timers. The governing interface rules demand finite explicit emits, a single unknown-write vocabulary, and caller operands only where a native meaning was verified; checker and emitter changes sit with other lanes, while runtime sources, tests, and this task's catalogue merges are owned here. Failures already available include sql::query_failed pairing operation and code strings, sql::commit_unknown keyed by transaction id for transactions, http::timeout holding timeout_ms, and http::transport_failed holding a phase string. Ingress today reads request bodies with no bound at all, answering read failures with fixed 400 and oversize payloads with fixed 413.
